turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It's a good prompt to have people adding more customers in seats. You talked about the importance to figure out the trial length and what to put in the trial and free and things like that. Is there anything that just has surprised you? Something you've learned from iterating on that comes to mind?
turns.zh: 这是个好引子，让人去加更多席位的客户。你聊了搞清楚试用时长和往试用、免费里放什么的重要性。有没有什么让你惊讶的？从迭代那个里学到什么，想得起来的？

turns.speaker: Ben Williams
turns.en: I wouldn't say surprised me per se, but it's something that I think it's perhaps obvious in retrospect and that is that companies of different sizes, of different complexities of different industries from those that are very highly regulated to the other end of the spectrum, they're going to take different lengths of time to need to evaluate properly. So being able to cater for those in some way, whether it might be dynamic trial lengths or whether it be trial lengths that are based on usage or things like that, I think it becomes really important. That's something to be thinking about for sure.
turns.zh: 我不会说特别让我惊讶，但有件事我觉得回过头看挺显然的：不同规模、不同复杂度、不同行业——从高度监管到光谱另一端——的公司，需要不同长度的时间来恰当评估。所以能以某种方式照顾到那些，无论是动态试用时长、还是基于使用量的试用时长，我认为变得真的很重要。那肯定是值得思考的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. That's a great learning. I know Elena talks a lot about how trials often, screw you because you don't give people enough time to really evaluate it a company, so that makes sense. Last tactical question that I wanted to touch on is around activation milestones. I'm doing a survey right now with Yuri that I think will come out before this episode airs. But anyway, in real time, I'm curious how you think about setting what the activation milestone is for a new Snyk user. So maybe just share briefly how you think about what is an activation milestone? Why is that important? And then how you define that for Snyk? What is the milestone of a user is activated for your product?
turns.zh: 太棒了。那是个很好的学习。我知道 Elena 经常聊试用常常怎么坑你，因为你没给人们足够时间真正在公司里评估它，所以说得通。我想碰的最后一个战术问题，是关于激活里程碑。我和 Yuri 正在做一个调查，应该会在这期播出前出来。但不管怎样，实时地，我好奇你怎么思考给一个新 Snyk 用户设定“激活里程碑”是什么。所以大概简要分享你怎么想“什么是激活里程碑”、为什么重要、然后你怎么为 Snyk 定义它？对一个用户来说，被激活的里程碑是什么？

turns.speaker: Ben Williams
turns.en: First of all, what is activation? So for us, activation is indicative of the team forming a habit around the usage of Snyk. And when I say the usage, I actually mean deriving core value, which is ultimately fixing vulnerabilities. It's not just logging in. It's not even just finding vulnerabilities, it's fixing vulnerabilities. So building a habit around that. And the reason I say team instead of using them is, and we actually base most of our definitions of activation engagement around teams. It's really important because ultimately security is a team sport. That team might be one person, which case a user is equivalent to team, but often a team is multiple people and we actually expect different people to fulfill different parts of the team activation journey. (01:20:17): We also want to enumerate aggregate level activity around fix that sometimes happens off-platform where we can't explicitly measure it at the user level. So in the activation process, we have set up moments, aha moments and habit moments and our habit moments that we define as a team being activated, it's related to fixing vulnerabilities within 30 days of team creation. And the reason that is chosen, it's because there is a significant correlation with downstream. And in that case with activation three month retention and retention again based on, again, not just coming back and logging in but still fixing. So teams, that fix of vulnerability within their first 30 days are much more likely to still be fixing three months later.
turns.zh: 首先，什么是激活？对我们来说，激活标志着一个团队围绕 Snyk 的使用形成了习惯。而我说“使用”，其实指的是获得核心价值，最终是修复漏洞。不只是登录。甚至不只是发现漏洞，是修复漏洞。所以围绕那个建立习惯。而我说“团队”而不是“用户”的原因是——我们其实把大多数激活、互动的定义都基于团队。这很重要，因为安全说到底是团队运动。那个团队可能是一个人，那样用户就等同于团队，但常常一个团队是多个人，而且我们其实期待不同的人去完成团队激活旅程的不同部分。(01:20:17) 我们也想枚举在修复上、有时发生在平台外、我们无法在用户级显式测量的聚合级活动。所以在激活过程里，我们设置了“设定时刻”“顿悟时刻”和“习惯时刻”，而我们把“习惯时刻”定义为团队被激活——它和“在团队创建后 30 天内修复漏洞”相关。选这个的原因，是它和下游有显著相关性。那是说，和“激活后三个月留存”相关，而那个留存同样基于——不只是回来登录，而是仍在修复。所以那些在头 30 天里修复了漏洞的团队，更可能在三个月后仍在修复。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's really interesting. I love that. How did you come up with that number? Was there a decision scientist that looked at some inflection of at 30 days, and it's probably not exactly 30 in real life, but it's like a nice round number that's close enough, right?
turns.zh: 那真的有意思。我喜欢。你是怎么想出那个数字的？是有个决策科学家看了某个 30 天的拐点？而且现实里它可能不正好 30，但这是个够接近的漂亮整数，对吧？

turns.speaker: Ben Williams
turns.en: Yep, that's it. So there absolutely was a decision scientist in involved thankfully. We had to collect a lot of baseline data first. So after we built out the data platform, we needed actually to wait for bit to build a good data set. We did a huge amount of quantum analysis, a lot of splunking of the data, applying ML models along with a bunch of supporting call research as well. But we started really with identifying the corpus personas and they used cases, different roles of different users within the team based activation journey, defining our retention metric, which is still fixing. It's whether a team is fixed. Along with natural usage behavior and expected natural usage frequency. And then we found the habit moment that ultimately most strongly correlated with improved long-term retention. And most of the numbers side of things came out of our ML ops platform. (01:22:19): But after that, we then worked back to figure out that's the habit moment. That's what we see as activation, but there's a set of steps that teams need to get there. So what's the aha moment before that? What's the setup moment and what are the individual steps that the team needs to go through to reach that set up moment? So that's the overall process and ultimately it's a really strong model that allows us then to feed in the set of user level behaviors that we know can influence those different steps on that path to activation.
turns.zh: 对，就是这样。所以幸好绝对有个决策科学家参与了。我们得先收集大量基线数据。所以建好数据平台后，我们其实得等一阵积累出好数据集。我们做了海量定量分析、大量对数据的 splunking、应用 ML 模型，再加一堆支持性的通话研究。但我们真的从识别语料人物画像、用例、团队里不同用户的不同角色、基于团队的激活旅程起步，定义我们的留存指标——仍是修复，是一个团队有没有在修复。连同自然使用行为和预期的自然使用频率。然后我们找到了最终和长期留存改善最强相关的“习惯时刻”。而数字那侧大多出自我们的 ML ops 平台。(01:22:19) 但在那之后，我们倒推：那是习惯时刻，那是我们视为激活的东西，但团队要到达那，需要有一组步骤。那之前的顿悟时刻是什么？设定时刻是什么？团队要经历哪些单独步骤才能到达那个设定时刻？所以那是整体过程，最终是个很强的模型，让我们能喂入那些用户级行为——我们知道它们能影响通往激活的路上那些不同步骤。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. I'm excited to get this post out and that's a really good anecdote of how a company comes up with it and what they set. What comes to mind?
turns.zh: 太棒了。我很期待把那篇 post 发出来，那真是个公司怎么想出来、又设了什么的绝佳轶事。我也刚想到另一个我可能开始问每个人的问题。我知道我老说要收尾了，但这里有个问题，如果不 work 我们就去掉。你提到一堆你们用的工具，我好奇，如果你要想到对你们组织最重要/最有价值的五个 SaaS 产品（除了 Salesforce 这种显然的），你会想到什么？

turns.speaker: Ben Williams
turns.en: When you say organization, do you mean Snyk at large or do you mean the growth?
turns.zh: 你说组织，是指 Snyk 整体，还是增长？

turns.en: Let's say, let's start with growth and see where it goes.

turns.en: Okay. So I'm going to say Amplitude, first of all. Segment as a means to be able to get our data from the products to Amplitude and to everywhere else that cares about it. turns.zh: 好。所以我先说 Amplitude。Segment，作为能把我们的数据从产品送到 Amplitude、以及任何别的在乎它的地方的手段。无论是下游 BI 系统、上面叠 Snowflake 和 Looker，还是像 Marketo 那样的市场自动化系统。所以我说 Amplitude。接下来我说 FullStory，对 session 回放当然绝对棒。它弥合了[听不清 01:24:11]之间的鸿沟。我会说 userinterviews.com，相当于 usertesting.com，两个都是超棒的服务，能快速、精选地接触到个人来参与用户研究。Sprig 是另一个。Sprig 是个超棒的 app 内调查平台，我们主要用它做这个，但它也做一堆别的酷事，比如能在 app 内测试 UX 设计。我说了几个了？

turns.en: I'll stick it at four.

turns.zh: 好。我喜欢这问题。我要开始问了。这太棒了。好。那是个前奏，非常刺激的快问快答。我就问你一堆快问快答，想到啥答啥。保持简短快。问题一：你会最常推荐给别人的一两本书是什么？

turns.speaker: Ben Williams
turns.en: I have been dreading this question as there are too many. So I'm pick a couple that I've enjoyed reading in recent months. So for product and growth geeks like me, or in fact anyone with more than a passing interest in data, I'll recommend "How to Measure Anything" by Douglas Hubbard. Second up, you had Marty Cagan and he mentioned the book "Sprint" by Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky and I love that book, but personally their "Make Time" book. It was something that radically changed my relationship with information and I recommend that to all time staff, product people out there. And for number three, I'm going to say, "This is How They Tell Me the World Ends" by Nicole Perlroth, which gives an amazing view into the world of digital espionage.
turns.zh: 我一直在怕这问题，因为太多了。所以我挑几本最近几个月读得开心的。对像我这样的产品和增长 geek、或者其实任何对数据不止随便感兴趣的人，我推荐 Douglas Hubbard 的《How to Measure Anything》。第二，你有过 Marty Cagan，他提了 Jake Knapp 和 John Zeratsky 的《Sprint》，我爱那本书，但个人更爱他们的《Make Time》。它彻底改变了我和信息的关系，我把它推荐给所有产品人。第三，我说 Nicole Perlroth 的《This is How They Tell Me the World Ends》，它给了数字间谍世界一个惊人的视角。

turns.en: Oh, I read that book. Tim Ferris recommended that at one point. That is a wild ass book. Very beautiful. Cool. I love these recommendations. All right. Great choices. Favorite podcast other than the podcast you're currently on
turns.zh: 哦，我读过那本。Tim Ferris 某时推荐过。那是本疯狂的书。非常精彩。酷。我爱这些推荐。好选择。除了你正在上的这档，最喜欢的播客？

turns.en: Maybe "Acquired" with Ben Gilbert and David Rosenthal. I just wish I had enough time to listen to them all.
turns.zh: 也许是 Ben Gilbert 和 David Rosenthal 的《Acquired》。我只是希望我有足够时间听完全部。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: They're very long. I was just at an event where they interviewed someone live as a live podcast. That was very cool. Those guys were pros. What's a favorite recent movie or TV show?
turns.zh: 它们很长。我刚在一个活动上看到他们 live 采访一个人，作为现场播客。那很酷。那俩是专业人士。最近最喜欢的电影或剧？

turns.speaker: Ben Williams
turns.en: Give a couple here if it's not cheating too much. First is one I like to ask when hiring for anyone actually really it's fast forward three years. What's different about you then? A lot of people will default to telling you where they aspire to be in terms of role or title, but what I'm really looking for is signals of humility, of self-awareness around areas of personal and professional growth. So people who can be open about where they think they need to work on to grow themselves as people. I love that. Also, so there's just generally throughout interviews, I'm looking for curiosity. So day-to-day good PMs will be asking why as much as my six year old son does, which is a lot. So I'll try and discern that through the course of the conversation. It's not really a question, but something I'm looking for. (01:28:27): And then maybe I want to flip it because building on something that Adam Fishman was saying, his theme of evaluating the people dimension of folks you are potentially going to work with when you're interviewing with a company. And this was a question I got asked myself recently by a candidate, which I just thought would brilliant, and that was, "Tell me about the diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging initiatives that you've recently personally been involved with?" And it just felt like a really great way for them to be able to test alignment of their personal values with those of someone they'd be working with really closely. So I love that.
turns.zh: 如果不算太作弊，我给两个。第一个是我喜欢在招聘任何人时问的：快进三年。那时的你有什么不同？很多人默认告诉你他们渴望的角色或头衔在哪，但我真正找的，是谦逊、对自身个人和职业成长领域有自我觉察的信号。所以能开放谈他们认为需要努力成长的人，我爱。还有，整个面试里我一般都在找好奇心。所以日常里好 PM 会像我六岁儿子那样频繁地问“为什么”——那可频繁了。所以我会在对话过程里试图分辨那个。那不算真问题，但我在找的东西。(01:28:27) 然后也许我想翻转它，基于 Adam Fishman 说的：他在面试一家公司时评估你潜在要共事之人的“人的维度”的主题。而这是我最近被一个候选人问到的、觉得超棒的问题：“跟我说说你最近亲自参与过的多元、公平、包容和归属感（DEIB）举措？”它就像个很好的方式，让他们能测试自己的个人价值观和那些会紧密共事之人的价值观是否对齐。所以我喜欢。
